The external IP 185.220.101.42 conducted reconnaissance via port scanning on 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), followed by lateral movement and successful authentication using compromised credentials. No malware was found in associated files, but behavioral analysis showed low-risk indicators. The breach remains active.

SIEM correlation identified 23 suspicious logins originating from 10.0.10.51 across Finance OU accounts. Pass-the-hash attack confirmed.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was initiated via a phishing email that delivered a malicious payload through an encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook. The payload executed a Cobalt Strike beacon via an unsigned DLL loaded from the Temp directory using rundll32.exe. The attacker established C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23 and began lateral movement using compromised credentials. The initial access vector originated from IP 203.0.113.88, which previously conducted a port scan on an IT workstation. Containment actions were denied due to lack of pre-approval, highlighting a gap in incident response authorization protocols.

arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected, originating from external IP 185.220.101.42. The attacker conducted reconnaissance via port scanning against an internal IT host (WS-IT-101), then pivoted to compromise 23 user accounts in the Finance OU using pass-the-hash. Despite detection and firewall blocking of the origin IP, attempts to revoke compromised credentials via IAM/PAM were denied due to lack of approval. This represents a high-risk gap in incident response authority during active breaches.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 initiated a port scan (Nmap SYN) against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Detected and logged by IDS.
Internal lateral movement observed: successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) as CORP\helpdesk. Pivoting established.
Multiple failed authentication attempts observed for Finance OU users (including j.martinez, s.patel, d.chen) from internal source 10.0.10.51. Indicative of pass-the-hash exploitation.
SIEM correlation confirms compromise of all 23 Finance OU accounts. Critical finding issued.
T8 IAM/PAM tool invoked to revoke all compromised credentials. Action denied due to approval requirement.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 185.220.101.42. Partial containment achieved.
EPP/AV tool escalation due to action limit reached during response attempts.
